claims.text: The untreated (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy exhibits a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation.
The untreated alloy has poor mechanical integrity and tends to crack.
Rapid solidification will produce a fine, metastable microstructure in (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38.
Tailored annealing after rapid solidification will form coherent nanoscale secondary-phase precipitates.
The processing route will generate a finely grained dual-phase microstructure.
Fine precipitates can contribute to strengthening in high-entropy alloys.
The proposed coherent precipitates will pin dislocations in (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38.
The refined grains and precipitates will strengthen grain boundaries.
The refined grains and precipitates will deflect cracks and impede crack initiation and propagation.
Rapid solidification and annealing will retain the phases responsible for the alloy's caloric response.
Excessive precipitate volume fraction or precipitate growth can degrade compressive performance.
Processing must avoid grain coarsening to preserve the proposed mechanical benefit.
The processed alloy will have greater compressive strength than the untreated alloy, potentially reaching at least about 152 MPa and approaching 218 MPa.
The processing route will significantly reduce cracking relative to the untreated alloy.
The processed alloy will maintain its caloric response within ±10% of the untreated alloy.
The mechanical and caloric benefits will coexist under the operational applied-field and pressure-field conditions.
The exact annealing temperature and duration needed for optimal precipitate formation are unknown and require experimental determination.

contradictions.description: The intervention is labeled a single-step thermomechanical route, but it explicitly consists of two sequential processing steps—rapid solidification followed by annealing—and no mechanical deformation step is specified.
The hypothesis says the intrinsic caloric effect will not be altered, whereas the predicted outcome permits a change of up to ±10%.
